title: Extensions worth knowing: query statistics, cryptography, geospatial

videos.script: PostgreSQL ships with less than it can do. {{list}} Forty-seven extensions sit on your server already, installed with the package and switched on in no database at all. Each one is a set of files on disk, and nothing happens until somebody types CREATE EXTENSION. {{create}} That command works per database. Install pgcrypto in one and the next database has never heard of it. {{perdb}} Some extensions need more than that. pg_stat_statements has to be loaded when the server starts, so it needs a line in the configuration and a restart. Get one letter wrong in that line and the server does not come back. {{typo}} This lesson installs three that a DBA meets on almost every server. pg_stat_statements, which counts what the application asks. {{top}} pgcrypto, which stores a password so that nobody can read it back. {{crypt}} And PostGIS, which comes from its own package and turns a pair of coordinates into a distance in kilometres. {{map}} Then it looks at what happens to all of them on the day the server is upgraded, because an extension is code somebody else wrote, and it has a version of its own. {{versions}}
